stories.headline: Total solar eclipse brings darkness across parts of Europe and Iceland
stories.body:
A rare total solar eclipse plunged parts of Europe into near-total darkness on August 12, 2026, creating a historic spectacle for millions of viewers [c11]. The astronomical event began at 15:34 GMT, with the period of totality lasting about two minutes [c10]. The path of totality passed over northern Russia, Greenland, Iceland, Spain, and part of Portugal, reaching approximately 15 million people [c11]. On the same day, people across parts of Africa were able to see a partial solar eclipse [c1].

Thousands of people gathered in Spain, Iceland, and other European countries to observe the sky [c5]. This event marked the first total solar eclipse visible in mainland Europe since 2006 [c12]. In Spain, it was the first total solar eclipse in more than a century [c6]. Spanish authorities expected at least 500,000 extra visitors to travel to viewing areas [c7]. The Spanish government estimated that 450,000 extra tourists would bring a 347-million-euro ($400 million) economic boost to the country [c13].

To maintain safety and manage traffic during the surge of visitors, Spain deployed more than 33,500 law enforcement officers around eclipse viewing sites and access points [c8]. Spanish Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska stated that nearly 25,000 police officers were mobilised for the event [c14].

Iceland also celebrated a major astronomical moment on August 12, 2026. The country experienced its first total solar eclipse since 1954 [c9]. In the capital city of Reykjavík, the total eclipse was visible for the first time since 1433 [c9].

The event deeply moved experienced space travelers. European Space Agency reserve astronaut Sara García Alonso told RTVE that the eclipse was one of the most beautiful things she had ever seen and gave her goosebumps [c3]. Astronaut Pablo Álvarez Fernández stated that the eclipse was much more beautiful than he had expected [c4].

People in the region will soon get another chance to see solar events. Another total solar eclipse is expected to cross southern Spain and northern Africa in August 2027 [c15]. That will be followed by an annular eclipse over the Iberian Peninsula in 2028 [c15]. However, after these events pass, the next total solar eclipse visible from the UK, France, and mainland Europe will not take place until September 2081 [c2].

vocab.meaning: the period of an eclipse when the sun is completely covered
related to space and celestial objects
brought together for a specific action or duty

stories.headline: White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt to leave role at end of August
stories.body:
White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt will step down from her position at the end of August 2026 [c16]. President Donald Trump wrote in a social media post that Leavitt will become one of his top outside advisors and an influential voice within the Republican Party [c17]. At age 28, Leavitt was the youngest person ever to serve as White House Press Secretary [c18].

During her time in the administration, Leavitt experienced several significant events. In February 2025, her office took control of the White House press pool from the White House Correspondents' Association [c21]. She gave birth to her second child, Viviana, with her husband Nicholas Riccio in May 2026 [c19]. She delayed her maternity leave that month following an alleged assassination attempt on Trump at the White House Correspondents' Dinner [c25].

Leavitt's departure follows the exit of four senior female Cabinet-level officials from Trump's second administration by mid-2026 [c26]. These included Kristi Noem, Pam Bondi, Lori Chavez-DeRemer, and Tulsi Gabbard [c26]. Before her White House role, Leavitt ran for a New Hampshire Congressional seat in 2022, winning the Republican primary but losing the general election to Democrat Chris Pappas [c20].

vocab.meaning: an election to select a political party's candidate
a government or head of state and their officials

stories.headline: Major earthquake in Colombia leaves hundreds dead and triggers rescue effort
stories.body:
A powerful 7.4-magnitude earthquake struck western Colombia at 07:34 local time (12:34 GMT) on August 10, 2026 [c35]. The epicenter was near San José del Palmar in Chocó province [c35]. Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella declared a state of emergency following the disaster [c38].

The earthquake caused widespread destruction across western Colombia. In Pereira, at least 92 buildings collapsed [c34]. According to the association Asocapitales, 79 people died in Pereira and 95 died in Cali [c33]. President de la Espriella stated that at least 265 people died and 496 remain missing [c32]. France 24 reported that more than 200 people were confirmed dead and over 2,000 were reported missing 48 hours after the disaster [c37].

Search and rescue operations continued as teams searched for missing people in the ruins [c36]. Emergency workers scored a dramatic success when 32-year-old Daniela Largo was rescued alive from the ruins of a collapsed hotel in Pereira [c39]. She had spent 36 hours trapped under the debris following the earthquake [c31, c39].

vocab.meaning: the point on the earth's surface directly above where an earthquake starts
scattered pieces of waste or remains from a destroyed structure

stories.headline: Tata Sons Chairman N. Chandrasekaran to step down in February 2027
stories.body:
Natarajan Chandrasekaran, the chairman of Tata Sons, has announced that he will step down from his leadership position at the end of his current tenure in February 2027 [c40]. The announcement marks the upcoming end of a decade-long leadership run at the top of one of India's largest business conglomerates.

Chandrasekaran stated that he decided to step down because Tata Sons board member Noel Tata did not support extending his term for a third five-year period [c44]. Noel Tata took on a major role in the group's leadership in October 2024, when he became chairman of Tata Trusts following the death of Ratan Tata [c42]. Former Tata Sons Chairman Ratan Tata died on October 9, 2024, at the age of 86 [c51].

The relationship between Tata Trusts and Tata Sons is central to the group's governance structure. Tata Trusts controls a 66% stake in Tata Sons [c43]. Meanwhile, the Shapoorji Pallonji Group holds approximately an 18% stake in Tata Sons [c45]. Under internal company rules, the leadership of these two entities is kept separate. Tata Sons amended its articles of association in 2022 to bar the chairman of Tata Trusts from simultaneously serving as chairman of Tata Sons [c47].

Chandrasekaran has spent his entire career within the Tata Group. He worked at Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) for 30 years, starting in 1987 [c41]. He served as the Chief Executive Officer of TCS from 2009 to 2017, before becoming the chairman of Tata Sons in January 2017 [c41].

His time leading Tata Sons was accompanied by high financial compensation. For the 2026 financial year, Chandrasekaran received a total remuneration of ₹158.66 crore from Tata Sons [c49]. That payment included ₹140.69 crore in profit-linked commission [c49]. Between the 2022 and 2026 financial years, Chandrasekaran earned a cumulative ₹671.4 crore in remuneration from Tata Sons [c50].

As Tata Sons prepares for leadership change, potential successors are being discussed. Tata Steel Managing Director TV Narendran is being considered among candidates to replace Chandrasekaran as Tata Sons chairman [c48]. Meanwhile, the group faces legal and administrative matters elsewhere. The Sir Ratan Tata Trust (SRTT) is currently unable to convene trustee meetings due to a directive from the Maharashtra charity commissioner [c46].

vocab.meaning: a large corporation formed by merging different companies
the period of time during which a person holds an official position

stories.headline: China calls border situation stable following reports of new standoffs with India
stories.body:
Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun stated on August 12, 2026, that the border situation between China and India is generally stable at the moment [c52]. The comment came after military standoffs and face-offs between Indian and Chinese troops emerged in the Taksing area of Upper Subansiri district in Arunachal Pradesh in early July 2026 [c53]. China claims large parts of Arunachal Pradesh as South Tibet, referring to the region as Zangnan [c59].

The two nations held diplomatic talks shortly before the spokesperson's statement. India and China held the 36th meeting of the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination on India-China Border Affairs in New Delhi on August 6, 2026 [c57]. On August 7, 2026, the Indian Union Home Ministry officially issued standard Indian names for 27 locations and geographical features in Arunachal Pradesh [c55, c58].

Tensions along the long frontier have flared in recent years. Clashes in the Galwan Valley in June 2020 killed 20 Indian soldiers and at least four Chinese soldiers [c54]. In October 2024, India and China reached a disengagement agreement covering friction points at Depsang and Demchok [c56].

vocab.meaning: a situation in which agreement or action is impossible; a deadlock
the withdrawal of military forces from a position of conflict
